text:
Sam Park: heads-up, getting a customer report: p95/p99 spike on text-generation API for the last ~10m, they see timeouts and many 429s. Their account is high-throughput (bursting).
Priya Rao: thanks, can you paste the request IDs or example timestamps?
Sam Park: example req id 0f8b7a3c, their logs show 'admit_rejected: concurrency_limit' and long queueing. Seen across eu-west1 and us-west2. Link to dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/latency?range=15m&service=text-gen
Elena Morales: I'm seeing a correlated spike in our admission_controller metric: concurrent_active ~2.5x usual and admission_queue_size spiking to ~1200. Worker pool cpu is fine but token processing lag per-worker increased.
Dan Kim: interesting — did we roll anything to runtime in last hour? deploy-bot: deploy completed by elena at 2145676000: runtime v3.9.1 -> v3.10.0 (kv-cache optimizations).
Elena Morales: roll looks green in e2e but maybe kv-cache change altered memory pressure leading to GC stalls on a subset of workers. GC-stall would cause backlog without raising CPU.
Priya Rao: customer says calls are mostly streaming completions with long contexts, high concurrent requests from same key. Could be client holding connections.
Sam Park: support repro: curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"model":"rwd-13b","prompt":"x","max_tokens":2048}' - run 50 concurrent. They hit 429 + p95 ~3.2s then 5xx.
Elena Morales: capturing logs on candidate workers: tail /var/log/redwood/runtime.log shows repeated lines: 
```
[2145678887] WARN admission: rejected request=0f8b7a3c reason=concurrency_limit active=512 limit=200
[2145678891] WARN runtime: hold on tokenization, kv-cache GC pause 48ms
```
Dan Kim: ok immediate mitigations: 1) temporarily increase admission_controller.per_client_burst to 400 for hosted tier (to prevent 429 for big customers) 2) enable fallback route to rwd-6.7b for that API key 3) trigger rolling restart of problematic workers to clear GC/heap fragmentation. Which one should I do first?
Elena Morales: I'd prefer fallback route first (safe) then restart small subset of workers (canary) — increasing per-client burst globally could worsen tail latency for other customers if we oversubscribe.
Priya Rao: customer asked for immediate relief; they prefer fallback to lower-cost latency model. I can update routing for their key. Can we do a canary that only affects that key?
Sam Park: yes please do that + tell them to throttle test volume by 20% while we stabilize.
Dan Kim: executing fallback patch now: routing.update(key=acct-9812, route=rwd-6.7b, reason="emergency fallback") -> done. Confirmed traffic for acct-9812 shifted to rwd-6.7b.
ops-bot: alert suppressed for acct-9812 after routing change.
Elena Morales: after fallback p95 dropped from 3.2s -> 1.1s for that key. admission_queue_size trending down but still higher than baseline.
Dan Kim: I'll start a rolling restart of the runtime ring in eu-west1, 5 pods at a time with 30s drain. Doing canary 1/5 now.
Sam Park: customer notified about fallback and restart, they're ok with canary restart.
Elena Morales: monitoring heap/GC on restarted pods. If GC pause >50ms persists after restart we need to revert kv-cache change or adjust cache size/eviction.
Priya Rao: documenting repro steps for SRE and support triage: 1) run 50 concurrent long-context streaming generates 2) watch admission_controller.admit_rejected 3) check runtime logs for 'kv-cache GC pause' 4) if seen, route affected key to smaller model or increase client-specific burst temporarily.
Dan Kim: can we also add a short-term mitigator: reduce default max_inflight_tokens per-request from 4096 -> 2048 for hosted public pool to reduce token-processing pressure? That would impact everyone though.
Elena Morales: I'd rather add a targeted throttle rule: if client concurrency > 200 AND avg_seq_len > 1024 then cap inflight_tokens for that key. Less blast radius.
Sam Park: agreed, add that rule and schedule a postmortem. Priya, can you update the ticket and ask the customer to share their load pattern if they can?
Priya Rao: on it, filing ticket REDW-4312 with timeline, mitigations, and asking for their replay script.
oname: oncall-bot: paging oncall uplink -> Dan Kim acknowledged.
Dan Kim: rolling restart finished in eu-west1, no regression observed. Global admission_queue_size down ~70% from peak. Still keeping the fallback for acct-9812 for 1h and watching.
Elena Morales: action items: 1) telemetry: add alert for kv-cache GC pause >40ms correlated with admission rejections; 2) runtime: implement per-key inflight_token cap rule; 3) product: consider per-key burst allowance UI in console; 4) SRE: schedule full ring restart during low-traffic window to defrag memory.
Sam Park: thanks team. Priya I'll keep customer thread updated and close after 24h stabilization. :thumbsup:
Priya Rao: thanks, will ping if they repro after we revert fallback later.
Dan Kim: saving logs and capture: /srv/triage/2145678901/ -> tarball created.
Elena Morales: leaving monitoring window open for 2h.
Sam Park: closing thread in slack but preserving context in ticket REDW-4312.
